doc.title: Rufus Reid interviewed by Monk Rowe, Atlanta, GA, January 4, 2013

title: Feel that can't be put in a book; young wunderkinds
summary: Some things can't be written in a book; he praises naturally savvy young players and conferences.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Yeah. And I think that’s a good thing.
Some of it has to come from the veterans and the players.

Yes. I mean to me this is why people even like the music is the way it feels. And so when we start making everything we do be put in a book, I mean I’ve written a book, but there are certain things that I just can’t put in a book because it’s impossible. Forget about it. And some people are looking for all the answers. They’re not there. And that’s where we were talking about creating those characters that somehow they just have a natural feeling for it. There are people who just come to things and they just understand. They have a savvy. And they’ve never done it before. But somehow — you see some of these young kids that are coming up now. They play like they’ve been on the planet for twenty years, and they’re only twelve. But they have a savvy. They just understand. We call them wunderkinds. We call them whatever. And sometimes people want to make them famous. Come on. And that to me is a drag. But they do have something. Just don’t squash it you know. And that to me is why I continue to come to these conferences and things, because it’s wonderful to see the hunger for some of the musicians. Because I used to be one of them.
